questions.question: What does Spanner's default external consistency add beyond replicas eventually agreeing?
options: Every query runs without network communication
Transaction order respects the order in which clients can observe commits finishing
All reads are served from the closest replica
Every table uses the same primary key
questions.explanation: External consistency gives transactions a serial order that also respects real-time commit order observed by clients.

questions.question: Why is a monotonically increasing timestamp a risky first primary-key part for a high-write table?
options: Spanner cannot store timestamps in primary keys
New inserts concentrate at one moving edge of the sorted key space
questions.explanation: Spanner range-shards rows by primary key. A monotonic leading value directs new writes to the same range until the hotspot moves with later splits.

questions.question: A migration must keep unique INT64 IDs, but their numeric order has no business meaning. Which built-in key strategy best matches that constraint?
questions.explanation: A bit-reversed positive sequence retains integer identity while distributing newly generated values across the key space.

questions.question: Which read mode asks Spanner for the newest consistent timestamp within a caller-defined age limit?
questions.explanation: Bounded staleness lets Spanner choose the freshest timestamp inside the limit. It is available only for single-use read-only transactions.

questions.question: In the lesson's five-voter base multi-region model, how many votes form a write majority?
questions.explanation: A majority of five voting replicas is three. Read-only replicas do not vote and do not increase this quorum.

questions.question: Why must a Spanner read-write transaction function avoid sending email or charging a card?
options: The database encrypts all outbound traffic
The client library can retry the function after an ABORTED attempt
External systems always use stale reads
questions.explanation: An eligible aborted transaction can rerun the callback. Non-transactional side effects inside it could happen more than once.

questions.question: What is the role of a read-only replica in a Spanner multi-region design?
options: It serves reads without voting on writes or becoming leader
It stores no data but votes on every write
It always serves strong reads without leader coordination
questions.explanation: A read-only replica maintains a full copy and serves reads, but it does not vote, join leader election, or become leader.
